records.application_period: Follows the SMU undergraduate admission cycle for international and other qualifications. For AY2026-27: applications opened 17 November 2025, 12.00pm Singapore Standard Time and closed 19 March 2026, 11.59pm, Singapore Standard Time, with standardised test scores due by 31 March 2026; shortlisted applicants attend an interview or test between March and May; actual final results must be submitted within 3 working days of release; admissions decisions are released May to July 2026, with second-window offer responses due by 16 June 2026; matriculation June to July 2026; classes start 17 August 2026. records.description: The ASEAN Undergraduate Scholarship is an SMU-administered award for applicants who are citizens of ASEAN member countries other than Singapore, applying for admission to a full-time undergraduate degree programme at Singapore Management University. SMU publishes 100% coverage of subsidised undergraduate tuition fees after the MOE Tuition Grant, plus an annual living allowance of S$5,800, an annual accommodation allowance of S$3,000 and a one-time computer allowance of S$1,750 on enrolment. The scholarship itself carries no bond, but because the tuition coverage is conditional on accepting the MOE Tuition Grant, every international recipient is placed under the Ministry of Education's 3-year bond to work for a Singapore-registered company immediately after graduation. Recipients must maintain a cumulative GPA of 3.0 out of 4.0, reviewed at the end of each academic term, and are liable to repay liquidated damages on breach.
records.best_fit: Applicants who are citizens of Brunei Darussalam, Cambodia, Indonesia, Lao PDR, Malaysia, Myanmar, the Philippines, Thailand, Timor-Leste or Vietnam, who hold outstanding high school results, show strong leadership and co-curricular records, and are applying for a full-time undergraduate degree programme at SMU.
records.eligibility_summary: Eligibility criteria published by SMU: citizens from ASEAN member countries (excluding Singapore citizens); have strong leadership qualities and potential; present good co-curricular activities records; possess outstanding high school results; be applying for admission to a full-time undergraduate degree programme at SMU. SMU lists the ASEAN member countries as Brunei Darussalam, Cambodia, Indonesia, Lao PDR, Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Timor-Leste and Vietnam. Recipients must maintain a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0 out of 4.0, reviewed at the end of each academic term, and may not concurrently hold any other scholarship, bursary or university loan without prior written approval from the University. Applicants with international qualifications must also satisfy SMU's general admission requirement of at least 12 years of formal education and submit one standardised test score.

records.name: Bourse du Gouvernement Français (French Government Scholarship)
records.official_source: French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs (Ministère de l'Europe et des Affaires étrangères), implemented by Campus France
records.duration: Awarded for a fixed period tied to the programme; the Licence-level rate applies for the duration of the degree.
records.deadline: "Quel que soit leur pays de résidence, les candidats doivent donc, avant leur départ et suffisamment à l'avance, s'adresser directement à ces services [Services de coopération et d'action culturelle des ambassades et des consulats généraux] situés dans leurs pays d'origine afin d'obtenir toutes les informations sur ces bourses : conditions d'attribution, calendrier de sélection, dossiers à constituer."
records.application_period: There is no single global application window. Each French embassy or consulate abroad sets its own selection calendar for the scholarships it awards, generally for the following academic year.
records.application_method: Not automatic on admission. The scholarship is applied for directly to the French embassy or consulate (Service de coopération et d'action culturelle) in the candidate's country of residence; separately, admission to a French institution is applied for through the national admissions platform for the degree level (the 'Etudes en France' platform, pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr, for first-year Licence applications).
records.description: The Bourse du Gouvernement Français is the umbrella status for French government scholarships awarded by the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs for study, internship and short research or language stays in France. Most of them are awarded by the cultural cooperation services of French embassies and consulates abroad rather than in Paris. Campus France implements the awarded scholarship and publishes the official rate grid: EUR 900 per month for a Licence (bachelor's) or Master's level scholarship and EUR 1,850 per month for a doctoral one. Holders are exempted from the CVEC student contribution and from enrolment fees for national and engineering degrees in public higher education establishments under the Minister for Higher Education, but training fees and other living costs remain with the holder.
records.best_fit: Foreign students from a country served by a French embassy or consulate that runs a French Government Scholarship call at Licence level, who have been admitted or are applying to a French higher education programme and who accept the reporting and attendance obligations attached to scholarship-holder status.
records.eligibility_summary: The award targets foreign students. It is not open to French nationals. Nationality rules, subject areas, eligible levels and selection criteria are set by the awarding embassy or consulate for each country, so eligibility is defined per country; the ministry reserves some specific programmes for particular nationality groups. Applicants must be admitted to or applying to a French higher education programme and must sign and honour the scholarship-holder obligations.

Licence-level French Government Scholarships are awarded by French embassies and consulates, not by the ministry in Paris through a single central call. 'Bourse du Gouvernement Français' is an umbrella status covering several categories (bourses d'études, bourses de stage, bourses de séjour scientifique de haut niveau); this record covers the bourse d'études at Licence level.

records.description: Since winter semester 2017/18 the state of Baden-Wuerttemberg charges international students from non-EU and non-EEA countries who hold a foreign university entrance qualification a tuition fee of EUR 1,500 per semester for Bachelor's and Staatsexamen programmes. Under Section 6 (4) and (5) of the State Higher Education Fees Act (LHGebG) the universities may exempt up to 5% of international first-semester students from this fee, fully or partially, on grounds of special aptitude. Heidelberg University operates this quota through its charter of 28 July 2017, and the waiver is granted by the Central Admission Committee of the Senate for International Students for the standard period of study of the enrolled degree programme.
records.best_fit: Non-EU/EEA applicants with a foreign university entrance qualification who have been admitted to a Bachelor's or Staatsexamen programme at Heidelberg University and who can document academic or school achievement beyond the normal German Abitur grade, special performance-based distinctions, or prizes and scholarships. The charter also directs particular consideration toward students from African, Caribbean and Pacific states and from least-developed countries.
records.eligibility_summary: Open to fee-liable international students at Heidelberg University, i.e. students who are not citizens of EU or EEA member states and who hold a foreign university entrance qualification (EU/EEA nationals and holders of a German university entrance qualification are exempt from the fee and so cannot benefit from this waiver). Applicants must be enrolled, or be about to enrol, in a grundstaendige (undergraduate) or Master's degree programme at the start of the approval period, must file a separate written application by the exclusion deadline, and must prove special aptitude (besondere Begabung). records.description: Dalhousie University publishes a single undergraduate entrance award programme, the General Entrance Award program (GEA), through which international students are considered for entrance scholarships, bursaries and hybrid merit/need awards. Dalhousie offers "more than 2,000 entrance awards (scholarships) each year" with an approximate yearly value range of "$1K to $80K", awardable one-time or renewable for up to four years. One GEA application puts a student forward for hundreds of awards, assessed on academic achievement, leadership and initiative, extracurricular involvement, community service, financial need and cultural identity, with each student assessed individually on the full application. Eligibility is explicitly open to international students: "All students—domestic and international—are eligible to apply." Applicants must be entering directly from high school (or be a mature student with no transferable post-secondary study), be starting in the Fall term, and meet the academic requirement, typically an 80% average or 26 predicted/anticipated IB points. Named international awards listed on the page include the CorpFinance International Limited (Kevin Andrews) Indian Scholarship ($15,000, Bachelor of Commerce, students from India), the Murray Family Jamaican Engineering Scholarship ($88,000, $22,000 renewable for 4 years, Bachelor of Engineering with preference for Civil Engineering, students from Jamaica, academic standing and financial need) and the international strand of the Sankofa Scholarships ($48,000, $12,000 per year renewable for 4 years, international student of Black/African descent from the Caribbean entering an undergraduate degree program). Awards are not a tuition waiver: they are applied to the student account in two equal instalments in mid-August and mid-December, and any residual after tuition and fees may be refunded.

Academic entry is assessed either through an Australian AQF Level 7 route or through published Year 12 equivalent percentage thresholds of 75% for most undergraduate degrees and 85% for Allied Health courses other than Nursing.

records.notes: SCOPE CORRECTION, stated plainly because the assigned award name was wrong. The b46 assignment row names a 'Jasminka Scholarship - University of Ljubljana'. No award of that name exists on the University of Ljubljana site. The University's own English scholarships page (https://www.uni-lj.si/en/study/scholarships, fetched 2026-10-03) lists only two University-run schemes for international students, the Residency of Prof. Grega Košak (a 4.5-month artist/designer/restorer residency, not a degree scholarship) and the Heart UL campaign (fundraising for enrolled students in financial emergency, not a tuition scholarship), and it refers all state scholarships for international students to the Public Scholarship, Development, Disability and Maintenance Fund of the Republic of Slovenia at srips-rs.si. 'Jasminka' is most plausibly a machine-generated garbling of the Fund's Slovenian name, Javni stipendijski, razvojni, invalidski in prezivninski sklad Republike Slovenije; that Fund is a different awarding body, so recording its Zois scholarships or its nationality-locked open calls (Western Balkans, Senegal/Nepal/East Timor, Angola, Ethiopia/Uganda/Rwanda, Türkiye refugees, Palestinian nationals) as a University of Ljubljana award would be a provenance error, and several of those calls are master's-only or locked to nationalities in excluded regions. This record therefore covers the only broad bachelor's-level funding instrument the University itself publishes: the statutory tuition-fee exemption for international students. It is a TUITION REDUCTION, not a scholarship: it is automatic on enrolment, has no application, no deadline, no competition, no stipend and no cash amount, and it applies only to the tuition fee. funding_amount is null on purpose: the University publishes the 2026/2027 tuition and study-contribution amounts as one PDF price list per faculty/academy plus separate lists for enrolment fees and study contributions, doctoral study and interdisciplinary bachelor programmes, and those PDFs were not opened for this record, so no EUR figure is recorded rather than inventing one. Those per-faculty tables mean the fee waived is field-specific in value, but the exemption itself is not restricted by field or faculty. No bond, service obligation or repayment clause is published; the exemption is a fee rule, and the conditions that can withdraw it (changing programme and enrolling in the same or a lower year after a repeat year, or re-enrolling in a programme previously withdrawn from) are recorded as award_holder_conditions. The same exemption rule covers full-time master's study; only the bachelor's level is recorded in degree_levels, and the doctoral level is explicitly excluded because the University lists all doctoral students as obliged to pay. records.description: Western University's Office of the Registrar offers an unlimited number of Welcome to Canada Admission Scholarships to international students entering full-time first-year study at its main campus. Each award is worth $10,000 for the first year and includes a guaranteed place in on-campus residence for the first two years of study. Consideration is automatic on admission and no application is submitted. The award may not be combined with any other admission scholarship, although the New to Canada Grant is payable on top of it.
records.best_fit: International students finishing secondary school outside Canada, or transferring into Western's main campus from a Canadian post-secondary institution, who are entering any first-entry undergraduate programme, are paying international tuition and fees, and can enrol full-time.
records.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be international students who completed school outside of Canada or are transferring from a post-secondary institution within Canada; students who completed high school within Canada are not eligible. Applicants must apply for first-year full-time studies (minimum 3.5 courses) in any first-entry undergraduate programme at Western main campus for the 2026-27 Fall/Winter academic year, must be paying international student tuition and fees, must meet the admission conditions in their offer, and must not defer the award. Reducing enrolment to part-time or withdrawing from the academic year forfeits eligibility, and any change in Canadian status that qualifies the student for domestic fees after an offer renders them ineligible.

records.english_requirement: Western's admission English language proficiency requirement (not a scholarship-specific test). IELTS Academic: minimum overall band 6.5 with a minimum of 6.0 in each section. TOEFL iBT for tests taken before 21 January 2026: minimum overall 83 with a minimum of 20 in each section. TOEFL iBT for tests taken on or after 21 January 2026 (1-6 scale): minimum overall 4.5, minimum 4.0 in reading, speaking and writing, minimum 4.5 in listening. PTE Academic: minimum overall 58 with a minimum of 56 in each section. Cambridge C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency: minimum overall 176 with a minimum of 169 in each section. CAEL: minimum overall 60 with a minimum of 60 in each section. Duolingo English Test: minimum 115 overall with a minimum of 100 in each subscore.
records.selection_notes: No selection committee, interview, essay or published weighting is described. The University publishes an unlimited number of awards and states that consideration is automatic, so there is no competitive ranking against a fixed quota. No academic-average threshold is published for this award on the award page read, unlike Western's automatic admission scholarship pool which uses admission-average bands.
records.notes: Chosen from several distinct international awards on the uwo.ca host. Western publishes an international entrance scholarship pool, three $100,000 International President's Entrance Scholarships, an $80,000 Neen Hodgins President's International Entrance Scholarship, and this Welcome to Canada Admission Scholarship. The Welcome to Canada Admission Scholarship was selected because it is the only one with its own dedicated official award page stating a precise, current benefit (CAD 10,000 first year plus a two-year residence guarantee), an explicit international-only eligibility rule, unlimited availability, and an explicit automatic-on-admission method - i.e. the best-documented award, not the highest-value one. No two records were produced for this host. Separately, the Automatic Admission Scholarships page publishes renewal conditions only for a former 'Western International Admission Scholarship' 'prior to the 2024-2025 academic year', indicating that named award was retired or renamed; no such award is claimed here. No renewal provision is published for the Welcome to Canada Admission Scholarship, which is stated as a first-year amount. This is a partial award: Western publishes an estimated year 1 international tuition and fees range of $48,000 to $64,400, so the $10,000 does not cover tuition. The University also publishes an international Tuition Fee Guarantee capping year-2-onward undergraduate international tuition increases at 4% per year.
